previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants, diastolic heart failure, and recurrent infections was admitted for acute heart failure exacerbation with bilateral pleural effusions and dyspnea. She was found to have a yeast urinary tract infection contributing to delirium, treated with IV fluconazole. During her stay, she developed transient atrial fibrillation attributed to volume overload, which resolved with diuresis. A cardiac catheterization revealed significant three-vessel coronary disease, but surgical intervention was deferred due to her complex medical status. She developed a right upper extremity DVT related to her PICC line, requiring anticoagulation with warfarin. Her immunosuppressants were adjusted due to acute kidney injury, which peaked post-catheterization but stabilized. She completed treatment for C. diff prophylaxis, and her mental status improved as metabolic and infectious factors resolved. She was transitioned from IV to oral diuresis with torsemide, and multiple medications were reconciled at discharge, including starting warfarin, metoprolol, and high-dose aspirin while discontinuing several others. She was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs and a plan for close outpatient follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
Acute venous embolism and thrombosis of superficial veins of upper extremity
Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile

This is a ___ old ___ female with a complicated past

#.Respiratory distress, hypercarbic - The patient presented with 
fever and increasing work of breathing with dyspnea that 
developed over ___ hours. She was started on empiric HCAP abx

extubated on ___.   
. 
#. CAD - Cardiac enzymes initially rose upon arrival to the

dysfunction c/w CAD; severe mitral regurgitation and moderate 
tricuspid regurgiation; compared with the prior study the 
estimated PA systolic pressure is now higher."" Cardiology was 
consulted and she had a cardiac catheterization on ___ - 
rotoblater used with DES to LAD. She tolerated the procedure 
well. On ___, she had ST elevation with a trop elevated to 
1.71. Cardiology was consulted and they did not want to stent 
her. She was started on lisinopril 2.5mg PO qday.  
.
#.Volume status ___ on CKD, CHF) - Difficult to manage given 
patient's renal failure and concominant severe mitral 
regurgitation. She was initially hypotensive and responded well

She was started on Lasix gtt at 15mg/hr for a goal of -1 to -2 
L. On ___, she received a tunnelled HD line for initiation of 
CVVH. She became hypotensive and did not respond to IVF, was 
startd on levophed on ___. On ___, her SBP was very labile 
and it was difficult to strike a balance of IVF and pressors. 
Her levophed was weaned off on ___.  Since coming to the 
floors, the patient's blood pressures were also labile and she 
was continued on HD ___ to assist with volume control.  She 
will be discharged to rehab with outpatient dialysis three times 
weekly for further volume control.
.
#. Fever- She was started on vancomycin and meopenem initially 
for presumptive HAP. Out of concern for possible varicella 
pneumonitis, her acyclovir dose was changed to a prophylactic 
dose. On ___ she spiked another fever to 38.2 and she was 
cultured. A urine culture resulted yeast in her urine and she 
was started on fluconazole. A blood culture resulted on ___ 
and showed GPC's in ___ bottles. Her IJ line was removed and the 
tip was cultured. Her A-line was also removed at this time.
.
#. CHF- the pt has known systolic CHF (LVEF-34-40%), was given 
lasix 20 IV at rehab and 20 IV in ED. Pt has reasonable responce 
(300cc within ___ hour).  This pt should not be aggressively 
diureses right now as she's in an early septic phase and will 
likely be pre-load dependent.  The  patient's volume status was 
managed with HD/ultrafiltration.  Patient's BPs have been very 
labile and so beta blockers were not initiated during this 
admission.
.
#. S/p renal/pancreatic transplant - She was continued on renal 
dosing of sirolimus and tacrolimus. Renal consultants were 
closely following her throughout her stay in the MICU. On ___, 
she began to develop LLQ pain. A renal US showed air in the 
transplanted kidney which is likely from her foley. She improved 
with no interventions necessary.  On transfer to the floor, the 
patient did not have any abdominal pain and the issue resolved.  
The patient's tacrolimus and sirolimus levels were followed 
every morning; she was initially continued on tacrolimus 2.5 mg 
BID, sirolimus 1.5 mg daily, and prednisone 5 mg daily.  
However, her tacrolimus was eventually increased to 3 mg BID.  
She will have to get her tacrolimus and sirolimus levels checked 
one time weekly as an outpatient.
.
#.A-fib with RVR - on ___, she developed afib with RVR and was 
started on IV metoprolol with PRN diltiazem. When she converted 
to sinus rhythm, she was started on amiodarone which was later 
stopped when she became bradycardic.  She again went into afib 
with RVR on ___ after CVVHD. As a result, her CVVHD was backed 
off.  The patient's Afib had resolved by the time she was 
transferred to the floor.
.
#Rash - disseminated rash developed 5 days prior to admission to 
MICU. ID was consulted and they recommended continuing acyclovir 
for concern of disseminated zoster. A sputum VZV was sent along 
with gram stain/culture. Dermatology was consulted and a biopsy 
was done which was consistent with an old varicella infection. 
She was taken off precautions.  As per ID recommendation, the 
patient will need prophylaxis with acyclovir at 200mg q12h.  
.
# acute kidney injury: The patient initiated dialysis during 
this hospital admission; likely secondary to acute tubular 
necrosis from decreased forward flow while she was pressor 
dependent in the MICU.  The patient's creat peaked at 3.6 and at 
discharge, her creat was 2.7.  The patient never had a post ATN 
diuresis that would be expected if her acute kidney injury 
secondary to ATN was resolving.  She was still making some urine 
on the medicine floor, however, only in small amounts (~50 cc 
over the course of 24 hours).  The patient will be discharged to 
rehab with outpatient dialysis follow-up.  The patient had a 
tunnelled line placed on R chest; it was not pulled when she 
developed her coag negative Staph bacteremia, but was treated 
with Vancomycin.  The patient's lisinopril was also discontinued 
given her acute kidney injury as well as her borderline low 
blood pressures.
.
# coag negative Staph bacteremia:  The patient was found to have 
coag negative staph bacteremia growing out of ___ bottles.  All 
of her lines were pulled, EXCEPT her tunnelled HD catheter line 
and it was decided to treat through the line.  The patient will 
be on Vancomycin, HD dosing, for a total of two weeks (started 
on ___ and will continue the vancomycin with dialysis 
until ___.  A TTE was done could not rule out valvular 
vegetations, and a TEE was done showing that the patient did not 
have any vegetations.  Please note, when getting the vanco 
trough, please make sure that trough is drawn AFTER the dialysis 
machine has been running for ___ minutes, as the patient's HD 
line is vanc blocked and we do not want that to be causing a 
falsely elevated trough.   
.
# yeast UTI: The patient was also found to have yeast growing 
out of her urine.  She was started on fluconazole 100 mg daily 
and will complete a two week course.  Antifungal sensitivities 
were sent to ___.
.
# vocal cord paralysis:  The patient was found to have vocal 
cord paralysis by ENT which can account for her weakened voice 
s/p intubation and her inability to drink thin liquids because 
would frequently aspirate.  ENT wanted a CT neck/chest to rule 
out any masses that were pressing on the laryngeal nerve that 
could be causing larygneal nerve dysfunction, especially given 
her immunocompromised status.  CT was negative for any masses.  
The patient will follow up with ENT as an outpatient.  Speech 
and swallow was following the patient while inpatient and she 
will be discharged on dysphagia/avoid thin liquid diet.
.
# Hypothyroidism -continued on home levothyroxine.

#. type 1 DM s/p pancreatic transplant, complicated by

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure taking care of you while you were hospitalized 
at ___.  You were initially admitted to the hospital because 
you were having shortness of breath at rehab; you had 
respiratory failure and you were admitted to the intensive care 
unit and connected to a machine to help breath for you. While in 
the intensive care unit, you were also found to have acute heart 
dysfunction and you underwent a heart procedure where a stent 
was placed in your coronary artery.  
.
Your blood pressures were very low and you needed medications to 
help support your pressures.  During this time, we think that 
your kidneys were not getting enough fluid, and you developed 
kidney dysfunction.  It was decided that you should start 
dialysis because of your poor kidney function, as well as to 
help stabilize your volume status.  
.
As you were leaving the intensive care unit, you were found to 
have bacteria in your blood.  You were started on antibiotics 
through your veins for this. Because bacteria in your blood can 
sometimes latch onto your heart valves, we did imaging of your 
heart; we did NOT find any bacteria latching onto your heart 
valves.
.
You also were found to have a urinary tract infection with 
yeast; we started you on an antifungal medication for this.  You 
need to take another four more days of this medication (STOP on 
___.  
.
You were also seen by the ears/nose/throat (ENT) doctors ___ 
___ were here because you were having some problems drinking 
thin liquids (instead of going into your esophagus, the liquid 
was entering your lungs).  They found that you had a problem 
with your vocal cords, and they want you to follow up with them 
as an outpatient. 
.
We made the following changes to your medications:
START Vancomycin with your dialysis until ___
START Fluconazole 100 mg daily until ___
STOP lisinopril
STOP carvedilol

CHANGE aspirin 81 to 325 mg daily
DECREASE acyclovir from 400 to 100 mg daily

INCREASE tacrolimus to 3 mg daily
INCREASE sirolimus 1.5 mg daily
STOP Coumadin until you see your PCP
STOP fosfomycin tromethamine
START Sevelamer 800 mg TID with meals

than 3 lbs.

INDICATION:  Shortness of breath, evaluate for fluid overload.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:  There is moderate pulmonary edema, increased compared to the
comparison radiograph from ___.  Concomitant infection at the
lung bases cannot be excluded, however.  There are small bilateral pleural
effusions, decreased in size.  Heart size is top normal.  The mediastinal
contours are unchanged.  There is no pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Increased moderate pulmonary edema.  Infection at the lung bases cannot be
excluded.

2.  Small-to-moderate bilateral pleural effusions, decreased compared to
___.

AP CHEST AT 10:28 A.M. ON ___

HISTORY:  A ___ woman with shortness of breath.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___ through ___:

Moderate-to-severe pulmonary edema has increased since ___ with
enlargement of moderate right and small left pleural effusion, diameter of the
cardiac silhouette and mediastinal veins, and both hila.  Followup is
recommended to confirm that what appear to be nodular opacities in the lung,
particularly the right upper lobe, resolved with improvement in the patient's
hemodynamic status.

HISTORY:  CHF versus pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, there is again enlargement of
the cardiac silhouette with diffuse bilateral pulmonary opacifications that
most likely reflect moderate-to-severe pulmonary edema with bilateral pleural
effusions, more prominent on the right.  The possibility of pneumonia as a
superimposing factor would have to be considered in the appropriate clinical
setting.

HISTORY:  PE versus pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, there is continued diffuse
bilateral pulmonary opacifications that could reflect substantial pulmonary
edema, widespread pneumonia, or even ARDS.  Pleural effusions persist
bilaterally.

HISTORY:  Tube placement.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the earlier study of this study, there has been
placement of an endotracheal tube with its tip approximately 3.2 cm above the
carina.  Nasogastric tube extends well into the stomach.  Diffuse bilateral
pulmonary opacifications are again seen.  Although this most likely reflects a
primarily pulmonary edema, the possibility of supervening pneumonia cannot be
excluded in the appropriate clinical setting.

PROCEDURES:
1.  Placement of a tunneled hemodialysis line.
1.  Placement of a triple-lumen central venous line.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ woman status post two renal transplants with
diastolic congestive heart failure and severe pulmonary edema.  Needs urgent
hemodialysis.

Informed consent for both procedures was obtained from the patient's
healthcare proxy over the telephone after risks, potential complications, and
benefits of the procedure were explained.  The patient was placed on the
angiographic table in supine position.  Skin of the right anterior neck, right
anterior chest wall, and left anterior neck was prepped and draped in a
sterile fashion.

ANESTHESIA:  Local.

After generous infiltration of the 1% lidocaine in the subcutaneous soft
tissues of the right anterior neck, under real-time ultrasound guidance, a
right internal jugular vein was punctured using 21-gauge micropuncture needle.
A 21-gauge needle was exchanged for a 4 ___ sheath over 0.018 guidewire and
followed by placement of 0.035 ___ guidewire into the right atrium through
the 4 ___ sheath.  Prospective measurement for the hemodialysis catheter
was obtained and appropriate 23-cm long line was selected.  A ___ 0.035
guidewire was advanced into the inferior vena cava.  4.0 ___ Kumpe catheter
facilitated cannulation of the inferior vena cava from the dilated right
atrium.  Attention was then diverted to the right anterior chest wall.  A soft
tissue tunnel was created in the subcutaneous soft tissues.  The dialysis line
was pulled through the soft tissue tunnel.  After appropriate dilatation of
the needle tract, the hemodialysis line was advanced through the appropriate
peel-away sheath into the right atrium.  Venipuncture incision was closed
using 4.0 Vicryl suture.  Tunneled line was secured to the skin surface using
0 silk sutures.

The attention was then diverted to the left anterior neck.  Fully compressible
and patent left internal jugular vein was identified using high-frequency
linear array transducer.  After appropriate infiltration of the subcutaneous
soft tissues by 1% lidocaine, left internal jugular vein was punctured using
21-gauge micropuncture needle.  The needle was exchanged for a 4 ___ sheath
over 0.018 guidewire.  A ___ guidewire was then placed through the 4
___ sheath into the right atrium.  Needle tract was dilated using 7 ___
dilator followed by placement of a 7 ___ triple-lumen central venous line
into the distal superior vena cava.  The line was secured to the skin surface
using 0 silk sutures.  Hemostasis was achieved.  Sterile dressing was applied
bilaterally.

CONCLUSION:
1.  Placement of a tunneled dialysis line into the right atrium via the right
internal jugular vein.
2.  Placement of a triple-lumen central venous line into the distal superior
vena cava via the left internal jugular vein.
3.  Both lines are ready to use.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with pulmonary edema and intubated.  Evaluate
for change.

PORTABLE AP CHEST RADIOGRAPH.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior chest radiographs from ___ and ___.

FINDINGS:  The patient is intubated with the ET tube 3.2 cm from the carina. 
A large bore right-sided catheter tip terminates in the region of the right
ventricle.  A left-sided IJ catheter tip terminates in the region of the mid
SVC.  An NG tube enters into the stomach but extends off the field-of-view. 
The cardiac silhouette is enlarged.  There are diffuse hazy bilateral
opacities, likely a combination of layering pleural effusions, pulmonary
edema, and possible consolidations especially in the retrocardiac region.  No
pneumothorax is present.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Worsening overall appearance to bilateral opacities in both lungs
suggestive of worsening edema.  Effusions and consolidations also appear
worse.
2.  Satisfactory ET tube position.
3.  Large bore right-sided catheter tip in the region of the right atrium.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with CHF.  Evaluate for interval change.

COMPARISONS:  ___.  ___.  ___.

FINDINGS:  Single frontal view of the chest was obtained.  A large right
pleural effusion, increased in size, slightly shifts the mediastinum to the
left.  Left retrocardiac dense consolidation with air bronchograms is
compatible with collapse of the left lower lobe.  Vascular congestion and
bilateral pulmonary edema has overall improved compared with ___. 
Endotracheal tube, right dialysis catheter, left internal jugular line, and NG
tube are unchanged in position.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Improved pulmonary edema and pulmonary vascular congestion.
2.  Slightly increased large right pleural effusion.
3.  Unchanged left lower lobe collapse.

PORTABLE CHEST, ___ AT 0400 HOURS

HISTORY:  CHF.

___ at 0304 hours.

FINDINGS:  Various lines and catheters remain in satisfactory position.  There
has been mild improvement in both the left lower lobe atelectasis and large
right pleural effusion.  Pulmonary vascular congestion and interstitial edema
are essentially stable.  There is no evidence of pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:  Modest interval improvement.

PORTABLE CHEST ON THE ___ AT 0338

HISTORY:  Pulmonary edema.

___ at 0403.

Usual lines and catheters are in good position.  Heart size and vasculature
are normal.  Lungs are clear and there is only a very small residual right
pleural effusion.

IMPRESSION:  Minimal residual right effusion, otherwise good postoperative
appearance.

HISTORY:  Dyspnea and mitral regurgitation.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, the monitoring and support
devices remain in place.  Mild right effusion is again seen, without definite
acute pneumonia.

INDICATION:  A ___ female with kidney transplant and new pain over
graft.

COMPARISON:  Transplant kidney ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS:  The transplant kidney is again seen in the left lower quadrant
measuring 10.8 cm in length.  There is no hydronephrosis.  There are several
discrete echogenicities seen within the transplant kidney, which were not
present on the prior ultrasound.  The appearance is suggestive of air within
the transplant kidney.  No perinephric collection is identified.  No renal
mass is seen.  A Foley catheter is seen within a collapsed bladder.

DOPPLER EXAMINATION:  Color Doppler and pulse-wave Doppler images were
obtained.  Sharp upstrokes are seen in the arterial waveform of the main renal
artery.  Appropriate venous flow is seen in the main renal vein.  Resistive
indices of the intraparenchymal arteries are 81, 76, and 76 in the upper, mid,
and lower poles respectively.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No hydronephrosis.  An echogenic pattern seen within the transplant kidney
suggests that air may be present in the collecting system.  If the Foley
catheter has been manipulated, then this could represent reflux air.  In the
setting of pain, however, air could indicate an infection.
2.  Patent renal transplant vasculature with mildly elevated resistive
indices.

Findings of air within the transplant kidney were conveyed to Dr. ___
___ at 2:30 p.m. on ___.

VENOUS MAPPING FOR AV FISTULA

INDICATION:  ___ woman with diabetes mellitus, status post kidney and
pancreas transplant, now becoming dependent on hemodialysis.  presenting for
venous mapping of bilateral upper extremities for possible AV fistula
placement.  History of failed AV fistula in the left upper extremity.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale and Doppler ultrasound images of bilateral upper
extremity veins were obtained.

FINDINGS:  The right cephalic vein is patent with diameters ranging from of
0.08 to 0.20 cm in the arm and 0.12 to 0.38 cm in the forearm.  The right
basilic vein is thrombosed.  The left cephalic vein is patent in the arm with
diameters ranging from 0.28 to 0.43 cm and is thrombosed in the forearm.  The
left basilic vein is patent with diameters ranging from 0.14 to 0.17 in the
arm and 0.12 to 0.17 in the forearm.  Bilateral subclavian veins are patent
with normal phasic flow.  Bilateral brachial and radial arteries are patent
with triphasic flow.  Of note, there are calcifications within the wall of the
right brachial and radial arteries.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Patent bilateral subclavian veins with normal phasic waveform.
2.  Patent right cephalic and right and left cephalic vein in the arm, patent
left basilic vein.
3.  Thrombosed right basilic vein and left cephalic vein in the forearm.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman with diabetes type 1, status post kidney
and pancreatic transplant with vocal cord paralysis.

STUDY:  CT of the neck without contrast.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:  Please note this study is limited secondary to lack of  IV contrast
administration due to the patient's kidney function.  With this limitation in
mind, there are no large masses in the neck. The left vocal cord is medialized
in position likely related to the known paralysis. A few small scattered nodes
are noted; evaluation being limited due to lack of IV contrast.     The
thyroid gland appears normal.  There are bilateral pleural effusions, right
greater than left.  Extensive vascular calcification of the vessels is seen in
the common carotid and cervical internal carotid arteries and in several
peripheral arteries. 
Fluid with some debris is noted in the esophagus which is mildly dilated-
correlate clinically. 
A 6.4-mm nodule is seen in the left lung apex which needs further evaluation. 
Degenerative joint disease changes, most prominent at C5-C6 and C6-7, are seen
in the cervical spine with no critical canal stenosis appreciated. 

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of large focal mass compressing on the  vocal cords or along
the course of the laryngeal nerves; assessment is limited due to lack of IV
contrast images.
2.  Bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than left.
3.  6.4-mm nodule in the left upper lung. Recommend dedicated Chest CT to
further evaluate. 
4.  Extensive vascular calcifications consistent with the patient's history of
diabetes. 
5.  Degenerative disk disease, most prominent at C5-C6 and C6-7.
Fluid with some debris is noted in the esophagus which is mildly dilated-
correlate clinically. 
Other details as above.
